heroHeadline: Houthi Drone Intercepted Near Mecca — First Alert on Holy City Since 2017 — as Pact Allies Confirm They've Received No Saudi Request
heroSubtitle: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed a Houthi drone launched from roughly 1,100 km away before it reached Mecca's restricted airspace on Sep 16, the first such scare since 2017; coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki called the holy city's security a "red line," while the Houthis deny targeting it. It came a day after a separate barrage wounded 13 civilians in Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif. AP reports Turkish and Pakistani officials say Saudi Arabia has still not made a formal request for military support, with an unnamed Turkish official citing unfinished "institutionalization" of the alliance; Pakistan's ISPR spokesman called the pact strictly "defensive" and "collective deterrence," even as PM Shehbaz Sharif offered rhetorical solidarity. Riyadh is instead seeking outside air-defense help from France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt after depleting its own interceptor stocks in the broader Iran war.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
